meetings.summary: The water commission reviewed the preliminary FY22-23 budget, focusing on how tight it is against revenue, the health insurance line, and the new garage debt. The budget vote was deferred until salaries are settled in executive session. The board also discussed annual meeting articles for a PFAS pilot study, a truck, computers, and equipment, then went into executive session.

budget_items.what_was_said: Staff presented a preliminary projected budget next to the prior year's estimate; the salaries figure is a placeholder pending executive session.
A commissioner worried the projected budget is very tight against last year's actual revenue, which was depressed by a wet season.
The new garage's principal and interest payments are the biggest change; later the debt line was found not to match a straight 30-year schedule and needs correcting.

Budgeted health insurance well exceeds what was actually paid. Commissioners debated trimming it versus budgeting for five eligible family plans, and concluded it should be fine-tuned before the final budget.
The water tank loan makes its final payment in 2022, freeing that amount the following year, before the water main loan is finished.
A small equipment replacement line exists in the budget; larger items are funded by annual meeting articles from the connection and equipment accounts.
Cell tower revenue, water service connection, and equipment and mains accounts are separate reserves from the operating budget.
The auditor previously cited a surplus; commissioners favored putting any extra into water main or other funds.
Projected revenue is somewhat above the budget, a cushion of roughly fifteen thousand.
The superintendent wants an article to replace a pickup with a utility body truck. Bids may be better than the state bid.

budget_items.topic: Computers, SCADA server and meter software
budget_items.what_was_said: The SCADA system is 12 years old and needs a server and software upgrade; meter reading software is reaching end of life.
An older loan from 2010 at a low rate with partial forgiveness runs to about 2031.
A commissioner asked what the actual figure behind the maintenance line is; staff said earlier miscoding inflated it, and it will be reviewed before the final budget.
A pilot study is a prerequisite for grant funding; earlier estimates were far lower and are expected to be higher now. Commissioners want cost and odds clarified before an article.
The state revolving fund provides low-interest loans, historically near zero, prioritized among applicants.
Options discussed: straight plow versus V plow, steel versus aluminum body, diesel versus gas.
Possible article for a used loader to replace the aging backhoe, paid from the water service connection account.

decisions.decision: Cell tower RFP bid opening postponed to March 9th after consulting the attorneys; letters sent to the two parties that pulled the RFP.
Budget vote deferred until after executive session finalizes salaries; the board will review and vote at the next meeting in two weeks.
Health insurance line to be fine-tuned before the final budget rather than cut to actual-plus-10 percent.
Maintenance line and other items to be reviewed and cleaned up for the next meeting.
The superintendent will contact the engineer firm about the PFAS pilot study cost and process before any article is drafted.
The superintendent will draft annual meeting articles with pricing for board review: pilot study, utility truck, computers and software.

what_happened.line: The water commission deferred its vote on the preliminary FY23 budget until salaries are settled in executive session, with a vote planned at the next meeting in two weeks.
Commissioners said the projected budget is tight against last year's revenue, which was depressed by a wet season, and the new garage loan payments are the largest change.
The commission chose to fine-tune the health insurance line before the final budget rather than cut it to actual spending plus a margin.
The superintendent will contact an engineering firm about cost and process for a PFAS pilot study, then draft annual meeting articles with pricing for a truck, computers and software.
The cell tower RFP bid opening was postponed to March 9 after the board consulted the attorneys.

why_it_matters: Water rates and the district's reserves depend on this budget, and a thin margin against revenue means a wet or dry season can change whether the district covers its costs.
The annual meeting articles for a PFAS pilot study, a truck and computer upgrades are spending that district voters may be asked to approve.
watch_next: The commission's next meeting, about two weeks out, where it plans to vote on the FY23 budget once salaries are final.
March 9, the rescheduled bid opening for the cell tower RFP.
